annotation.kind: source-faithful reindexing of the repeated-matrix-power bound in Lemma 2.2

assumptions: X is a real n-by-n matrix whose entries are floating-point inputs.
Each matrix product is computed entry by entry using sequential rounded dot products under the standard relative-error model, excluding overflow and underflow.
The supplied X is the exact first power; k counts the further rounded multiplications, so the paper's exponent is t=k+1.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P23 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P23 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p23_t1_lemma_2_2 (fp : P23FPModel) (n k : Nat) (X : P23Matrix n) (hvalid : P23GammaValid fp.u (k*n)) : forall i j, abs (p23RoundedPowerSteps fp X k i j - p23PowerSteps X k i j) <= p23Gamma fp.u (k*n) * p23PowerSteps (p23AbsMatrix X) k i j
formal_statement.plain_language: After k rounded matrix multiplications starting from X, the componentwise error in the computed power is bounded by gamma_(k*n) times the corresponding entry of the (k+1)st power of |X|.

informal_proof: Induct on the number of multiplications. At each step split the new error into the local rounded matrix-product error and propagation of the preceding power error, bound both componentwise by products of absolute-value matrices, and combine gamma_n with gamma_(k*n) using the standard gamma addition rule.
informal_statement: Lemma 2.2 with t=k+1: repeated floating-point multiplication computes X^(k+1) with componentwise error at most gamma_(k*n)|X|^(k+1).

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: The importable matrix-multiplication theorem is the single substantial result: it supplies the full n-term floating-point dot-product analysis at every power step. The power induction and gamma arithmetic remain task-specific supporting work. Mathlib has no floating-point matrix-multiplication or repeated-power error theorem, and the closer Paterson-Stockmeyer source module is not in the frozen importable object set.
